Uttlesford's population increased by around 11,900 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 91,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Uttlesford increased by 15.0%, from around 79,400 in 2011 to around 91,300 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the East of England (8.3%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Uttlesford was home to around 1.0 person per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 0.9 in 2011. This area was among the lowest 15% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Uttlesford than across the East of England

Median age in Uttlesford

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Uttlesford increased by one year, from 42 to 43 years of age.

This area had a higher average (median) age than the East of England as a whole in 2021 (41 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by around 3,500 (an increase of 21.4%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 200 (1.1% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.1 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Uttlesford stood out from other areas for housing

The percentage of households in the social rented sector increased in Uttlesford, but fell across England.

In Uttlesford, the percentage of households in the social rented sector rose from 12.6% in 2011 to 13.0% in 2021, while across England it fell from 17.7% to 17.1%. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 15.7% to 15.5%.

Private renting in Uttlesford increased from 13.1% to 14.5%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 71.6% to 70.6%.

The rate of social renting in Uttlesford increased by 0.4 percentage points

Unpaid care in Uttlesford

In 2021, 4.6% of Uttlesford residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.7% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care was greater in Uttlesford (3.1 percentage points) than across the East of England (2.8 percentage points, from 7.3% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Uttlesford decreased by 3.1 percentage points

Religion in Uttlesford

In 2021, 41.5% of Uttlesford residents reported having "No religion", up from 26.2% in 2011. The rise of 15.3 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Uttlesford. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the East of England, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.9% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 50.2% of people in Uttlesford described themselves as Christian (down from 64.4%), while 5.8% did not state their religion (down from 7.4% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

In 2021, 41.5% of usual residents in Uttlesford reported having "No religion"

Uttlesford residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 81,100 Uttlesford residents said they were born in England. This represented 88.8% of the local population. The figure has risen from just over 71,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 89.8% of Uttlesford's population.

Scotland was the next most represented, with around 1,200 Uttlesford residents reporting this country of birth (1.4%). This figure was down from just under 1,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.6% of the population of Uttlesford.

The number of Uttlesford residents born in Wales fell from around 750 in 2011 (0.9% of the local population) to around 700 in 2021 (0.8%).

In 2021, 88.8% of Uttlesford residents reported their country of birth as England

National identity in Uttlesford

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater in nearby South Cambridgeshire (2.7 percentage points) than in Uttlesford (0.5 percentage points).

In Uttlesford, the percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity increased from 4.2% in 2011 to 4.7% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby South Cambridgeshire increased from 6.8% to 9.5%.

The percentage of people who identified with a UK and non-UK national identity in Uttlesford increased from 0.8% to 1.5%, while the percentage of people who identified as "British only" increased from 16.0% to 57.9%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Uttlesford increased by 0.5 percentage points

People looking after their family or home in Uttlesford

In 2021, 4.5% of Uttlesford residents (aged 16 years and over) said they were economically inactive because they were looking after their family or home. This figure was at a similar level in 2011 (4.4%).

The percentage of people who were economically inactive because they were looking after their family or home increased from 4.1% to 4.6% across the East of England. Across England, the percentage increased from 4.0% to 4.8%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were looking after their family or home (economically inactive) in Uttlesford increased by 0.1 percentage points

Health in Uttlesford

In 2021, 54.1% of Uttlesford residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 51.2% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.0% to 32.9%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Uttlesford residents describing their health as "very bad" remained 0.7%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 2.7% to 2.4%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

In 2021, 0.7% of usual residents said their health was very bad in Uttlesford

Fewer adults working long hours

Uttlesford saw the East of England's largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week (from 18.1% in 2011 to 14.4% in 2021).

Central Bedfordshire (from 14.9% to 11.7%), South Cambridgeshire (from 14.9% to 11.7%), Babergh (from 15.4% to 12.2%) and East Hertfordshire (from 16.6% to 13.4%) saw the East of England's next largest decreases in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week.

Every local authority area across the East of England saw a fall in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week, as the regional percentage fell from 14.3% to 11.9%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults in employment who worked 49 hours or more in Uttlesford decreased by 3.7 percentage points

Family in Uttlesford

Of Uttlesford households, 18.4% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 21.0% in 2011.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater in Uttlesford (2.6 percentage points) than across the East of England (1.8 percentage points, from 19.0% to 17.2%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Uttlesford decreased by 2.6 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Uttlesford residents aged 16 years and over, 29.4% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 26.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in two people (53.2%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 56.0% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Uttlesford that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 8.6% to 9.2%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater across the East of England (3.7 percentage points, from 31.1% to 34.8%) than in Uttlesford (2.8 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Uttlesford increased by 2.8 percentage points

Disability in Uttlesford

In 2021, 4.6% of Uttlesford residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 5.9% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 12 people (8.6%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 8.5% in 2011. The proportion of Uttlesford residents who were not disabled increased from 85.6% to 86.8%.

This area had the region’s lowest proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. St Albans had the East of England's next lowest proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot (4.8%), while Great Yarmouth and Tendring had the region's joint highest proportion (9.7%).

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Uttlesford decreased by 1.3 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Uttlesford

In 2021, 2.2% of Uttlesford residents identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category, up from 1.2% in 2011. The 1.0 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the East of England, the percentage of people from "Mixed or Multiple ethnic groups" increased from 1.9% to 2.8%, while across England the percentage increased from 2.3% to 3.0%.

In 2021, 94.5% of people in Uttlesford identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 96.6% in 2011), while 1.9% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 1.4% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 0.5% in 2011 to 0.8% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 2.2% of usual residents in Uttlesford identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category
